en.name: Lentils, dried
en.summary: Dried lentils keep about 1 year from purchase, and about 1 year again once the bag is opened and they go into a sealed jar. They do not need cooking soaked or stored cold, and what ends them is age-hardening rather than spoilage.
en.pantry: An airtight jar in a cool, dark, dry cupboard is all they ask, and that gives about 1 year from purchase — the same 1 year applies from the day you open the bag, provided you decant rather than rolling the top over. Two slow problems and one fast one: light bleaches the colour, oxygen turns the small amount of oil in the seed, and pantry weevils arrive much faster than either. The important thing about old lentils is that they harden: a bag well past its year is safe to eat but takes longer to cook and may stay stubbornly firm, which matters most with the whole types. Red split lentils, which collapse anyway, hide it best.
en.fridge: No refrigerator timeline is published for dried lentils and they do not need one — a dry cupboard already covers a year. In a hot, humid kitchen an airtight jar in the fridge is a reasonable precaution against damp and insects; just bring it back to room temperature before opening so condensation forms on the jar rather than on the lentils. Cooked lentils are a different food and should be cooled quickly and refrigerated in a covered container.
en.freezer: No freezer figure is given for dried lentils. Freezing a sealed bag for a few days is a genuinely useful way to deal with insect eggs in a bulk purchase, but it is a pest measure and not a shelf life, and it will not soften lentils that have already hardened with age. Cooked lentils freeze very well and are the more useful thing to keep in a freezer.
spoilage: Live weevils, small moths, webbing or fine dust in the jar.
A musty or mouldy smell, which means damp has got in.
Lentils that stay hard after a long simmer — an age problem rather than a safety one.
Grit, stones or shrivelled seeds, which are a quality issue worth sorting out before cooking.
tips: Decant into an airtight jar and date the lid on the day you buy them.
Rinse and pick over lentils before cooking; small stones are common.
Cook old and new lentils separately — they will not finish together.
Buy red split lentils if your stock turns over slowly; they cope with age better.

faq.q: How long do dried lentils keep?
faq.a: About 1 year from purchase, and about 1 year from opening in an airtight jar.
No, unlike most beans. But old lentils harden with age and may need much longer simmering.
Generally yes, if kept dry and free of insects. The problem is texture, not safety.

zh.name: 乾扁豆
zh.summary: 乾扁豆從購買日起算約可放 1 年，開封後倒進密封罐同樣約 1 年。它不需要泡水才能煮，也不需要低溫保存；終結它的是隨年紀變硬，而不是腐敗。
zh.pantry: 它要求的只是一個密封罐、一個陰涼避光乾燥的櫥櫃，這樣從購買日起算約 1 年——只要你一開封就換裝密封罐（而不是把袋口捲起來），開封後同樣約 1 年。兩個慢問題加一個快問題：光線讓顏色褪掉，氧氣讓種子裡少量油脂變質，而櫥櫃裡的米象來得比這兩者都快。關於老扁豆最該知道的一件事是它會變硬：放超過一年的豆吃起來安全，但要煮更久，而且可能一直硬，整顆的品項尤其明顯；紅色去皮的扁豆反正會煮化，最容易掩蓋這件事。
zh.fridge: 乾扁豆沒有公布的冷藏期限，它也不需要——乾燥的櫥櫃本來就有一年。濕熱的廚房裡，密封罐放冰箱是防潮防蟲的合理措施；只要開封前先回到室溫，讓水氣凝在罐子上而不是豆子上。煮熟的扁豆是另一種食物，要快速降溫並加蓋冷藏。
zh.freezer: 乾扁豆沒有給冷凍數字。把密封袋冷凍幾天，是處理大量採購蟲卵的實用做法，但那是防蟲措施不是保存期限，而且救不了已經因為年紀變硬的豆子。煮好的扁豆非常耐凍，那才是更值得放冷凍庫的東西。
spoilage: 罐內出現活的米象、小蛾、絲網或細粉屑。
聞到潮霉味，代表濕氣跑進去了。
煮很久還是硬——這是年紀問題，不是安全問題。
混有砂石或乾癟的豆粒，煮之前應該先挑掉。
tips: 買回來當天倒進密封罐，並在蓋子上寫日期。
煮之前先沖洗並挑一次；小石頭很常見。
新豆舊豆分鍋煮——它們不會同時煮好。
消耗慢的話買紅扁豆；它比較不怕放。

faq.a: 從購買日起算約 1 年；開封後放密封罐也是約 1 年。
不需要，這一點和大多數豆類不同。但放久的扁豆會變硬，可能得煮很久。

faq.q: 放很久的乾扁豆還能吃嗎？
faq.a: 只要一直乾燥、沒生蟲，通常可以。問題在口感，不在安全。
